soft_issues: Consensus_signal: The metadata states 'high_agreement', but the extract indicates some uncertainty and reliance on expert judgment, which could be flagged as ambiguous.
Controversy_role: The metadata states 'foundational', but given the reliance on expert judgment and semi-quantitative methods, this could be seen as debatable.

[regraded from critical] Missing COI: The metadata states 'no conflicts of interest declared', but the summary mentions funding by the Norwegian Environment Agency, which should be noted as a potential COI.

[offline_accept] Fabricated numbers: The summary states '51 out of 109 populations' affected by escaped farmed salmon, but the extract mentions '51 of 109 Norwegian populations show significant farm introgression'.

claim_checks.claim: Semi-quantitative 2D ranking (effect × development, 2015): escaped farmed salmon highest on both axes (~0.83 effect, ~0.80 development)—largest expanding population threat.
claim_checks.extract_quote: Escaped farmed salmon had the highest scores along both axes, and was identified as the largest threat.

claim_checks.claim: Salmon lice second expanding population threat (~0.70 effect, ~0.58 development); may render populations critically endangered (>75% adult reduction or >10% farm introgression) with high likelihood of further loss.
claim_checks.extract_quote: Salmon lice were identified as expanding population threats with high scores along both axes.

claim_checks.claim: 2015 Norway: ~382 million farmed salmon vs ~522,000 wild spawners (~732:1); worst-case >1 billion lice larvae day⁻¹ possible under regulations (Taranger et al. 2015).
claim_checks.extract_quote: In 2015, there were 382 million farmed Atlantic salmon... the number of wild adult Atlantic salmon returning to Norway the same year was estimated at 522,000 individuals.

claim_checks.claim: Experimental smolt protection studies: additional marine mortality from lice 0.6–39% across sites/years; large reductions in returning adults in affected populations (>25% typical).
claim_checks.extract_quote: Studies... have shown average additional marine mortalities by salmon lice of 0.6–39% across locations and years.

claim_checks.claim: Stabilized threats: G. salaris, acidification, hydropower/habitat alteration; overexploitation downgraded after conservation-limit management.
claim_checks.extract_quote: The introduced parasite G. salaris, acidification, hydropower regulation and habitat alterations were identified as stabilized population threats.

claim_checks.claim: 51/109 Norwegian populations show significant farm introgression (mean 6.4%, max 42%; Karlsson et al. 2016); lice risk moderate–high on parts of coast per national risk assessments.
claim_checks.extract_quote: Karlsson et al. (2016) recently documented that 51 of 109 Norwegian Atlantic salmon populations showed significant genetic introgression from farmed salmon.

evidence_direction_note: The evidence direction 'supports_effect' is consistent with the extract, which identifies escaped farmed salmon and salmon lice as major threats.
